source.title: IMAE for Noise-Robust Learning: Mean Absolute Error Does Not Treat Examples Equally and Gradient Magnitude's Variance Matters
source.authors: Xinshao Wang; Hua Yang; E. Kodirov; D. Clifton; N. Robertson

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test and training-subset accuracy as synthetic label-noise rates increase, bearing on V4, but does not test fitting completely random labels or the other listed versions.
record.gate_note: Table 6 reports test, noisy-subset and clean-subset accuracies for CCE, MAE and IMAE on CIFAR-10 at 0%, 40% and 80% label noise. These bear on V4. The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) and Arpit et al. (2017) for other claims; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures fitting of corrupted and clean training labels and test accuracy under increasing uniform label noise. These results test V4 under fixed training budgets and different losses; completely random labels are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. More precisely, the authors argue that MAE underfits meaningful patterns and is noise-tolerant because it emphasizes medium-probability examples, rather than weighting all examples equally. IMAE adjusts gradient-magnitude variance to improve fitting while retaining noise robustness; CCE progressively overfits noisy labels.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies partial synthetic label corruption and robust loss functions, rather than fully random labeling under the original memorization setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise rate, loss function and backbone change training-subset and test accuracies.

fits_no_version.finding: Hybrid accuracy combines clean training examples with test examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A combined measure of retaining meaningful labels can compare robust objectives, but does not separately measure training interpolation or test degradation.

record.peer_reviewed: Published at ICLR 2023 Workshop on Trustworthy and Reliable Large-Scale ML Models
record.problems: Only 0%, 40% and 80% noise are reported for CIFAR-10; the all-random endpoint is not tested. Training accuracies are substantially below perfect at corrupted settings. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 6 has 90 metric entries across losses, rates and backbones. Kept 60, prioritizing V4 and non-perfect/partial training accuracy results; omitted remaining test-accuracy and hybrid-accuracy entries and all 0%-noise rows beyond the first 15, which do not directly evaluate corrupted-label fitting.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error at that endpoint, and chance test performance without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Time to convergence relative to true-label training and its dependence on corruption fraction; all CIFAR-10 runs use a fixed 100k-iteration budget.
The all-random endpoint, a dense enough noise sweep to establish smoothness, and whether longer training would eventually interpolate. Uniform corruption here replaces labels with other classes.
Controlled removal or addition of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation, including generalization after their removal.

A demonstrated temporal ordering of real-pattern acquisition before noise memorization. The supplied figure captions and discussion describe progressive noisy-label fitting but do not establish that ordering.

missing.what: ResNet56 omitted corrupted-label training results: IMAE at 40% noise, noisy/clean accuracy 6.5/93.1%; at 80% noise, CCE 52.5/62.3%, MAE 9.6/15.6%, IMAE 13.0/44.7%. These are not covered by the stated omission of test/hybrid metrics and clean-endpoint rows.
missing.locator: Table 6, ResNet56, 40% IMAE and all 80% training-subset cells

missing.what: Training-dynamics evidence: CCE increasingly fits the noisy subset while test accuracy deteriorates; MAE and IMAE show smaller best-to-final test gaps. Add qualitative trajectory rows, without inventing unreadable curve coordinates.
missing.locator: Section 5.3.2, first results bullet; Figures 4 and 10

missing.what: Own CCE ResNet44 results on CIFAR-100: test accuracy 70.0%, 60.4%, 53.2%, and 42.1% at symmetric noise rates 0%, 20%, 40%, and 60%. This additional dataset bears on the degradation component; training interpolation is not reported.
missing.locator: Section 5.1; Table 3, Our Trained Results, CCE

missing.what: IMAE parameter sensitivity: at 40% corruption, fitting first improves as T rises from 0 to 8, then worsens at 16. IMAE-4 fits comparably to IMAE-8 but generalizes worse; IMAE-16 fits worse but generalizes slightly better. Numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Supplementary Sections B.2 and C.2; Figures 6b and 7b

record.verdict_notes: All training-subset values are final-model accuracies against the assigned training labels. Being below 100% alone does not establish absence: substantial but incomplete memorization is partial. The fixed training budget supports a scope qualification, not a claim that these networks cannot eventually fit noise. Omitted test/hybrid metrics and clean-endpoint rows already declared in rows_left_out are not independently flagged as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling and chance test error.
Training-time comparison to true labels and convergence slowdown by corruption fraction.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Noise rates between the reported rates and the all-random-label endpoint; the study does not report perfect training accuracy across the noise sweep.
Removing weight decay, dropout or data augmentation and evaluating their necessity or sufficiency.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels, or whether real and random labels are learned differently over training.

source_check.notes: The tested CIFAR-10 noise rates are 0%, 40%, and 80%; complete random labeling and eventual interpolation beyond 100k iterations are untested. The authors-conclusion paraphrase is faithful; several verdict endpoints are supported directly by Table 6 despite missing corresponding record rows.

statements.correction: For this study: limits_scope. ResNet20 noisy-subset accuracies at 40%/80% noise: MAE=6.8%/9.7%; IMAE=5.5%/16.8%. Training stops at 100k iterations. Section 5.3.2 reports substantially less noisy-subset fitting.
statements.problem: The suppression claim and training budget are correct, but a challenges label overstates this study's evidence of incomplete fitting under deliberately robust losses.
